title: COLLABMEM: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Collaborative Memory Operations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
reason: 核心贡献是面向多智能体持久记忆的诊断基准。评测固定交互轨迹、目标角色、答题者、裁判和金标准事件，以定位共享、访问、路由、溯源、冲突消解和保留问题。所提图记忆在五个划分上的非 Oracle 平均分最高（69.6%），为显式设置可见性、来源、权威性和保留规则提供了设计依据；摘要未报告各机制的独立效果。
abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly rely on persistent memory to coordinate role-specialized work. Correctness requires more than recalling a fact: the fact must reach the right role, remain hidden from unauthorized roles, carry the right source, and update when a more authoritative value appears. We introduce COLLABMEM, a diagnostic benchmark for collaborative memory operations. Its matched memory-only harness fixes the trace, target role, answerer, judge, and gold event, localizing errors to sharing, access, routing, provenance, conflict resolution, or retention. COLLABMEM contains 58 hand-authored scenarios (1,118 core probes), a 174-scenario scaled split (3,359 probes), adversarial and compositional hard sets, and six transactive-memory competencies. We also propose TMS-GRAPH++, a scope-aware graph memory framework with role-filtered views, writer/provenance structure, and temporal [CURRENT] marking. Across five evaluation splits, TMS-GRAPH++ achieves the highest non-Oracle average score (69.6%). Evaluations using the official SDKs of Mem0, Letta, and A-Mem show that shared archives help, but reliable collaborative memory still requires explicit visibility, provenance, authority, and retention policies. We will release the dataset, evaluation code, and reproduced outputs to support future work on multi-agent memory systems.
evidence: We introduce COLLABMEM, a diagnostic benchmark for collaborative memory operations.
result: Across five evaluation splits, TMS-GRAPH++ achieves the highest non-Oracle average score (69.6%).
